what: A census of the AMBER element at the front corners of real parked and moving cars in downtown Sarasota (side-marker, turn-signal or parking-lamp lens, lamps OFF, daylight), read only from the Mapillary panoramas in reference/sarasota/mapillary/. Per car, three questions: (1) is any amber visible at a front corner; (2) where it is, its linear-luma brightness over the car's own paint beside it on the same panel orientation (lens p50 / paint p50), and its internal spread (p90/p50); (3) its apparent size against the headlamp beside it, in pixels, on the same car in the same frame. The paint family and the light on the measured panel are recorded for every row, because the ratio depends on both.
method: SURVEY. Contact sheets of the horizon band (y 440-760, half scale) of all 202 panoramas and of the 27 flat frames. About 160 candidate sightings were zoomed at x2-x14 (about 330 zoom views); many were the same parked car in neighbouring frames. Zooms used tools/paint-tone.mjs --grid and scratch helpers that draw the same original-pixel grid; the helpers are placement aids, not measurements. Most zoomed vehicles were rear views, too distant, occluded, blurred, or repeats of one parked car.

DEDUPLICATION. Panoramas 5-15 m apart repeat the same parked cars. Each vehicle was tracked across frames by the capture position in mapillary/index.json and by appearance, and counted once (see "duplicates"). The best frame was used.

Q1, PRESENCE. A corner counts as amber when a connected cluster of pixels sits on the lamp or marker itself, with HSV hue 0-50 deg, saturation >= 0.25 and value > 0.12, and the zoom shows it is a lens rather than paint, ground, background or a reflection. The hue window includes red-orange because these JPEGs render amber lenses at a mean hue of 8-28 deg. "No amber" required a headlamp at least ~25 px wide with the corner resolved. Over the headlamp-plus-corner box, the largest amber cluster had to be <= 9 px, or any larger cluster had to be shown on a zoom to lie on background, a wheel-arch edge or foliage. The 4 measured positives give 43-71 px on the same test. Head-on views answer for the front face only and are marked as such.

MEASUREMENT. node tools/paint-tone.mjs --sample <frame> --boxes <lens>;<paint>, unchanged (sha256 89edc2df54156d06...). It was run from a scratch working directory with a symlink to reference/, so the tool's annotated crop went to scratch and docs/shots/ was not touched. The tool decodes the JPEG in Chromium (playwright 1.56.1), applies the exact sRGB EOTF per channel and takes Rec.709 linear luma per pixel. It reports p10/p50/p90 per box and the share of pixels with any channel at 255. lensOverPaint = lens p50 / paint p50, both in the same frame, so exposure cancels.

BOXES. The lens box sits inside the amber element: seeded on its saturated core and sized to its sat >= 0.25 extent where that is >= 4 px tall, never on the chrome or housing around it. The paint box sits on the nearest unbroken painted panel facing the same way: fender or bumper side for a side marker, the fascia directly below for a front-corner amber. It is clear of shut lines, badges, the wheel arch and specular streaks. Every box was checked on the annotated crop the tool writes, at about x10. One first paint box on the black Explorer had landed on the road behind the car; the crop showed it and the row was refused.

PLACEMENT SENSITIVITY. Both boxes were shifted by every (dx, dy) in {-1, 0, 1}^2, giving 9 lens x 9 paint = 81 ratios, all through the tool. The range is min-max, and spread = (max - min) / lensOverPaint. Spread <= 25% is "tight". 25-50% is "wide", kept and flagged. Over 50%, or lens p90/p50 > 2 (the box mixes the lens with something else), the row was refused.

REFERENCE SENSITIVITY. A second paint box on the same panel orientation, further from the lens, was read through the same tool. It is reported as altPaintBox / altLensOverPaint. A first alternate on the Compass sat where the fascia turns away into shade; it read 2.47 against 1.40 and was replaced, because it is a different orientation.

SIZES. Amber w x h is the bounding box of the 4-connected cluster of amber pixels (hue 0-50, sat >= 0.25; >= 0.40 where noted) seeded on the lens box, cross-checked by eye on the zoom. Headlamp w x h is the bounding box of the headlamp assembly as it appears in the same frame, including an integrated amber section, read off a gridded zoom to +-2 px. Both are apparent, projected sizes from one viewpoint.

LIGHT. From the cast-shadow direction on wider context views. "light" is the light on the MEASURED PANEL: sun, shade or dapple. "scene" says what the rest of the frame is doing. Three white or dark cars are in a sunny scene but photographed on their own shadow side, so they are classed shade.
caveats: This is photographed luminance, not albedo. The lens is a glossy curved plastic over a reflector, and its reading depends on what it mirrors (sky, ground, the next car) as much as on its colour. Paint carries clearcoat sheen and, on dark metallics, mirrors the sky: the Tacoma's grey fender reads bluish, mean sRGB 40,50,69.

The rows order by paint tone, so white cars read below 1 and dark cars above. That is the signature of a ratio whose denominator varies far more than its numerator. The family field is not optional context; it is half of the number.

Lit lamps: a daylight-lit amber would read near-clipped and saturated. Only one kept lens clips at all: the Jeep Compass, 2.8% of its box, a specular highlight visible on the crop. All three moving cars (Accord, CX-30, Rogue) read below their paint, which is consistent with unlit lenses. A dim lit element cannot be excluded.

Box size: the kept lens boxes hold 20-50 px. A box under about 4x4 px is dominated by JPEG 4:2:0 chroma subsampling, which smears a 4 px element's colour over about 8 px; such elements were refused (CR-V 7x4, Tesla strip 3-4 px tall).

JPEG floor: at L < ~0.03-0.05 (deep shade, black paint) a 1-code change is several percent of the reading, and black paint mirrors the ground. Both black cars with visible amber were refused for this.
Clipping: white paint in direct sun clips, and a ratio against it is only an upper bound (the Sequoia was refused).
The presence test cannot work on red or orange paint, whose own hue falls in the amber band (red Wrangler, GR86).

Wide rows (25-47% placement spread): Compass (a specular highlight on the lens); Mazda5 left side (a blurred outline); Mazda5 right side (a diagonal stripe 4-5 px thick); Tacoma (a strip 4-5 px tall over paint near the dark floor); Tundra (an 8x7 core inside a peach lens, over dark paint); Rogue (a diagonal band with dark gaps). Their first decimal place is the claim; the second is not.
The second paint box moves a ratio by 1-18% (median 15%). That is the size of "which part of the panel counts as beside it", separate from the +-1 px placement range.
Families are by eye. The Mazda5 is a warm silver (mean sRGB 151,134,117 in sun) and could be called champagne. Model names are identifications by eye, given only to help find the car.
Sizes are apparent. Side-view rows see the headlamp side-on, with its front foreshortened, so the amber/headlamp ratios mix viewpoints and come with no distances.

Sample: 9 measured cars from one ~1.5 km downtown corridor (Bayfront to Five Points) on one day (2024-10-13, one 360-camera rig), mostly 2015+ vehicles. No black or red car and no pre-2010 car survived measurement.
measuredBy: a census subagent, 2026-10-15 (summary recomputed from the lists and every row re-measured through the unchanged tool, 2026-10-17)

instrument.statistic: Rec.709 luma of sRGB-EOTF-linearised pixels; p10/p50/p90 by nearest rank; clipPct = share of pixels with any channel at 255
instrument.boxFormat: [x, y, w, h] in the original image's pixels

summary.derivation: Every count, median and quoted number in this summary is computed from the rows, noAmber and refused lists in this file when it is written; an independent audit re-derives each one.

amberOverHeadlamp.note: Apparent sizes in the same frame, from the raw pixel sizes of each row (not the rounded per-row ratios). The amber bounding box is a median 0.41 of the headlamp's apparent width and 0.50 of its height (n = 10 rows). Its pixel count is a median 0.082 of the headlamp bounding-box area (n = 9): a strip, chevron or corner wedge rather than a block. mazda5-silver-L is an eye-read bounding box, because its connected cluster leaks into a warm ground reflection along the bumper; it has no pixel count and is not in the area figure.

readThisFirst: lensOverPaint orders by paint tone: white 0.43-0.94 < silver 1.05-1.41 < dark grey 1.77 < dark blue 2.75 (white 4 rows / 4 cars, silver 4 rows / 3 cars, dark grey 1 row / 1 car, dark blue 1 row / 1 car). That is what a lens whose brightness depends far less on the body colour than the paint does would produce. A single number across families is therefore not a property of the lens. Compare within a family, or multiply by the family's own paint reflectance. The independence is an inference from the ordering: absolute lens values cannot be compared across frames, because each frame has its own exposure.
Light moves it too. The same Mazda5 reads 1.41 on its sunlit side and 1.05 on its shaded side, a factor of 1.34 on one car, so compare rows within a family AND a light.
No black or red car survived. On black paint the reference is at the JPEG floor and reflects the ground. On red or orange paint the paint itself falls inside the amber hue band.
A head-on view misses the side marker. The Expedition shows no amber on its front face but has an amber side marker; the 3 head-on "no" cars are front-face answers only.
